input.claim_text: On 8 February 2024 my son was kicking a soccer ball in the backyard and it smashed straight through our sliding glass door. The whole pane shattered and we've had to board it up until it can be replaced. I think it'll cost around $650 to fix.

output.cause: soccer ball kicked into sliding glass door

input.query: Coverage for accidental breakage of glass doors/windows caused by family members

input.query: accidental damage to glass windows or doors cover

output.answer:
Based on the excerpts provided:

**For fixed glass (e.g., windows) — only if "Home" is on your Certificate of Insurance:**

The RAA Contents PDS provides an Additional Benefit for "Accidental breakage of glass and sanitary fixtures." If **Home** is shown on your Certificate of Insurance, this covers the cost of repairing or replacing any part of fixed glass forming part of the Insured Property, including windows, if accidentally broken [RAA Contents PDS, page 52].

**For Contents cover:**

If **Contents** (rather than Home) is shown on your Certificate of Insurance, this Additional Benefit only covers glass forming part of:
- furniture;
- pictures, paintings, prints and mirrors designed to be hung from a wall or freestanding; or
- aquariums,

if accidentally broken [RAA Contents PDS, page 52]. This means fixed glass windows are **not** covered under this Additional Benefit if only Contents is shown on your Certificate of Insurance — the window/door glass benefit applies specifically to the "Home" category.

**Exclusions that apply regardless:**

This cover does not apply to:
- repairing scratches (where the break does not extend through the entire thickness of the item);
- glass in a glasshouse or greenhouse;
- repair or replacement of any tiles or tiled fixture or splashback (whether tiled or glass) forming part of the Home;
- toilet seats;
- glass forming part of a stove, heater, oven or cook top as a result of direct application of heat;
- a picture tube or screen of a television or visual display unit; or
- glass forming part of a radio or clock, vase, ornament, lamp or photo frame [RAA Contents PDS, page 52].

**On doors specifically:**

The excerpts do not explicitly mention "doors" in relation to this glass breakage benefit — only "windows" is specifically named under the Home category [RAA Contents PDS, page 52]. I cannot confirm from these excerpts whether glass doors are included or excluded, as the text does not address this directly.

**Note:** If you are asking about accidental damage under a separate "Accidental Damage" Optional Cover (as referenced on pages 41, 52, and 60), the excerpts provided do not include the specific terms of that Optional Cover in relation to glass breakage — they only reference its Sum Insured limits and interactions with other benefits [RAA Contents PDS, page 41, 60]. If you need details on how the general Accidental Damage Optional Cover treats glass, please provide those specific excerpts, as they are not included here.

Since coverage of the specific damaged item (glass door) is ambiguous based on the available policy text, and the claimed cause (accidental breakage by a kicked ball) could reasonably be covered but the policy language doesn't explicitly confirm doors are included, this meets the escalation criteria for contradictory/ambiguous coverage text. A human reviewer should confirm whether "fixed glass" in the RAA Home benefit extends to sliding doors before a payout decision (approve/deny) is made.
